name: Hōryū-ji bracketed timber structures
description: Japanese temple structures used a Chinese-derived post-and-lintel bay system, with brackets transferring heavy tiled roof loads to wooden columns.

date.label: Late seventh to eighth century CE
date.basis: The cited source reports this approximate period or year; archaeological contexts date associated remains rather than a unique invention.

events.statement: The Hōryū-ji temple area preserves late-seventh- and eighth-century timber structures using bracketed bays.

evidence.supports: The Hōryū-ji temple area preserves late-seventh- and eighth-century timber structures using bracketed bays.

contributions.group: Builders of the Hōryū-ji temple area

evidence.supports: The source describes Builders of the Hōryū-ji temple area and this contribution.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest sourced date for the specific documented case; this does not establish invention or worldwide priority.

caveats: UNESCO supplies a broad period for the complex, not a dated first use of the framing system; individual buildings and rebuilding histories vary.

research.note: Independently checked UNESCO’s broad site chronology and Chinese-derived bay framing. Buildings have differing histories and the broad period does not date the original adoption of each feature.
